question: Should experimental Claw lifecycle ownership diagnostics become a supported core Doctor surface once the prerequisite ownership stack lands?
rationale: The implementation is a new operator-facing core capability built on an open RFC and unmerged stacked contracts; technical validation cannot determine permanent product ownership or support expectations.

options.title: Sponsor the gated core diagnostic
options.body: Accept the core direction after the prerequisite ownership PR lands and require the documented read-only and advisory contracts to remain explicit.

options.title: Defer the stacked Claws surface
options.body: Keep this PR and its dependent slices unmerged until maintainers decide the lifecycle model and support boundary together.

options.title: Decline the core direction
options.body: Close the stack if maintainers do not want Claw lifecycle ownership and reconciliation to become a core OpenClaw responsibility.

recommendation.title: Defer the stacked Claws surface
recommendation.body: Keep this PR and its dependent slices unmerged until maintainers decide the lifecycle model and support boundary together.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared-state and Doctor architecture work makes this person the best available decision owner for the core persistence and support boundary.
